_: The schema's node kinds, the frame a packet travels in and the container a chunk is saved in, as data.
What each kind is on the wire is written in gen/docs/protocol.mc26tmpl.md, which
mc26 docs renders for a version into the data repository; the build checks that every
kind here has its section there. This file keeps what machines read: the list of kinds
with a one-line summary, the frame as data, which the recording proxy follows, and the
region file as data, which the JSON-only reader opens a world with.

data._: The frame as data, for a generator: the prose in `wire` and `fields` is the evidence, this is the description. gen/internal/capture (the recording proxy) reads its state changes and its compression and encryption triggers from here.

length.counts: every byte after it in the frame: the data length when compression is on, then the payload

id.note: an index into the table packets.json gives for the connection's state and the direction

body.fields: the packet's node tree in packet_schema.json, read to the end: nothing may be left over

enabledBy.on: the threshold is 0 or more; negative turns it off

dataLength.zero: the body follows as it is
dataLength.else: the body's inflated size, and the payload is a zlib stream (RFC 1950 framing, default level) of it

compression.compressWhen: the body, id and fields together, is at least threshold bytes

server: dataLength >= threshold when dataLength is not 0

enabledBy.then: the 16-byte shared secret the client chose is the key and the iv

encryption.scope: every byte of the stream in each direction from then on, the length prefix included; one cipher per direction, never reset; the server's stream from the moment it has read minecraft:key, the client's from the moment it has sent it

transitions.note: the field is the enum ClientIntent, sent as its own id: 1 STATUS, 2 LOGIN, 3 TRANSFER

states.note: each direction swaps its table on its own: the server's clientbound table changes when it sends the packet the client acknowledges (login_finished, finish_configuration, start_configuration) and its serverbound one when the acknowledgement arrives. Following the serverbound acknowledgements is right for both directions, since the server sends nothing in the new state before it has the acknowledgement.

bits.summary: Nothing new: exactly the bytes of the primitive named by `of`.

counted.summary: Exactly N repetitions of `elem` with NO count of its own in front of them; N is the value of an earlier sibling field of the enclosing struct, named by `count`.

dispatch.summary: The dispatch key, then — with no separator, length prefix, tag or padding — the whole payload of the codec that key selects; the union itself contributes no terminator and no size.

either.summary: One boolean byte, then exactly one of the two branches: non-zero selects `left`, zero selects `right`.

enumset.summary: A fixed bit set of exactly ceil(N/8) bytes with no count and no length prefix, N being the number of constants — the size comes from the enum's arity, which both peers must know.

guard.summary: Not a node kind — a key ON A STRUCT node holding the internal name of a Java enum.

holder.summary: Without "direct" (holderRegistry, 127 nodes): one VarInt registry id, no offset — holderRegistry delegates to the same private registry(key,Function) → ByteBufCodecs$29 as the registry kind.

lenprefixed.summary: A var int giving the number of bytes that follow, then one `elem` inside exactly those bytes.

list.summary: A var int count, then exactly that many `elem` values back to back, nothing between and nothing after.

map.summary: A var int count, then that many entries, each the key immediately followed by the value, no separator and nothing after.

nbt.summary: Exactly one NBT tag in network form — a 1-byte tag id then that tag's payload with NO root name and no length prefix; tag id 0 (TAG_End) is the whole value and carries no payload.

optional.summary: One boolean byte — 0 absent, any non-zero present, writers emit exactly 1 — then one `elem` when present and nothing when absent.

packed.summary: `entries` values of `width` bits each, packed into big-endian 64-bit longs with floor(64/width) values per long and no value crossing a long: value i is bits (i mod vpl)*width ..

prim.summary: Whatever prims.json defines for the name in `t`.

ref.summary: Nothing of its own — a back-pointer, not a byte.

registry.summary: One VarInt and nothing else — the numeric id of an element, written with no offset, no prefix and no length.

resourcekey.summary: Exactly one Identifier — a STRING (VarInt byte count then that many UTF-8 bytes) holding a namespaced id.

rest.summary: `elem` repeated until the enclosing window is exhausted, with no count anywhere: the number of repetitions is whatever fits, and a reader knows it has read the last one because the window has no bytes

string.summary: Identical bytes to the primitive token STRING — a VarInt BYTE count then that many UTF-8 bytes.

stringenum.summary: A STRING holding the constant's serialized name — VarInt byte count then that many UTF-8 bytes.

struct.summary: The concatenation of its fields in the order listed, and nothing else — BUT only for the array-`when` form.

when.summary: Not a node kind — a key ON A FIELD of a struct node (26.2 field key-sets are exactly {name,type}x2489 and {name,type,when}x40).

whilelist.summary: Entries repeated with NO count anywhere: each entry carries a continuation bit inside one of its own fields, and reading ends at the first entry for which the `while` condition holds.

region._: The container a saved chunk is stored in, as data: Mojang's RegionFile. One file per 32x32 chunks, named r.<x>.<z>.mca under the dimension's region/ directory; entities/ and poi/ use the same container. gen/crosslang reads a world from this and save_schema.json alone.

sector.note: the file is a whole number of sectors; the first two are the tables

entry.offset: the high 3 bytes: the chunk's first sector, 0 when the chunk is absent
entry.count: the low byte: how many sectors it spans

locations.index: x + z * 32, x and z the chunk's position inside the region

entry.value: seconds since the epoch when the chunk was last written

length.note: big-endian; counts the compression byte and the data, not itself

compression.external: a code with bit 0x80 set means the data is in c.<x>.<z>.mcc next to the file, in that compression

chunk.data: the NBT of the chunk: one unnamed TAG_Compound, the format save_schema.json describes as "chunk"
